newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss watch exports continue decline.
newsitem.headline: Swiss watch exports continue decline.

text.p: Swiss exports of watches continued to decline in 1997, falling by 1 percent in the first two months of the year, the Federation of the Swiss Watch Industry said Monday.

Against a backdrop of a weak Swiss franc, the federation said the outlook was relatively optimistic for the rest of 1997 and that the decline appeared to have stabilised, the Swiss news agency ATS reported.

Exports of watches totalled 1.12 billion Swiss francs ($772 million) in the first two months of 1997. They fell 1.5 percent in 1996 to 7.55 billion Swiss francs ($5.2 billion). That came after a 3.6 percent drop in 1995.
Finished watches accounted for more than 90 percent of the exports in the first two months of 1997 and were worth nearly 1 billion Swiss francs ($690 million), the federation said.
The biggest fall in the number of units exported was in finished watches -- down 20 percent to 5 million pieces.
In a sign of consumer interest in cheaper products, exports of steel, aluminium and base metal watches rose slightly in value, the federation said but gave no breakdowns for sales.

Asia, led by Hong Kong, remained the biggest market for Swiss watches and watch components with a regional share of 41.3 percent of all foreign sales in value, followed by Europe with 35.5 percent and the United States with around 14 percent.

ATS quoted Pierre-Alain Berret, head of the industry federation's economic office, as saying that prospects for global sales were favourable in 1997, notably in Asia, but that the market in Europe remained depressed.
